(2) āyoga and pratiyoga are obscure here: kept as printed (literally "application/assignment" and "counter-application"); not glossed further. (3) pratipakṣe vā-asya paṇyam enaṃ kariṣyāmi: asya taken with pratipakṣe ("in his rival side"); enam = him; the persons are not named. (4) mitram aparuddhaṃ vā-asya pratipādayiṣyāmi: aparuddha rendered literally "shut out" (glossary 12.1 gives "in disfavour" for a prince); asya taken as "to him"; it could also be "his ally ... I shall hand over". (5) khani-dravya-hasti-vana-setu-bandha-vaṇik-pathān: grouping uncertain ("produce-forests and elephant forests" is possible). (6) grāhayiṣyāmi = causative of grah, "make him grasp/take up". (7) tad ... pratipatsyate: subject not stated (the ally/support?); amitra-virakta could be "estranged from the enemy" or "alienated by the enemy"; tat-kulīna = member of his family (glossary). (8) The first iti (after dāsyāmi) is internal and is rendered by a dash, the second closes the quotation and is not rendered. "[ones]" supplied. The e-text puts "-" in āyogena-ārādhayiṣyāmi and vā-asya/vā-asmai (unsandhied joins). REVIEW: (a) printed paraṃ may be a typo for paraḥ (subject of kopayiṣyati); no text_flag could be added. (b) In "mitram aparuddhaṃ vā-asya" and "mitram āśrayaṃ vā-asya" vā may link two objects ("an ally or an aparuddha / an ally or a support"); the rendering "shut-out ally" is literal and unsettled. (c) khani-dravya-hasti-vana: dravya-vana and hasti-vana may be the pair "[produce]-forests and elephant forests"; kept literal. A person should check the whole plan.
why: reviewer (minor): parallel with "mitram āśrayaṃ vā-asya" suggests "an ally or an aparuddha" (vā linking two objects); draft reads aparuddha as adjective of mitram; param may be a typo for paraḥ; person to decide
